description: Find a motif NOBODY TYPED: given a set of sequences (multi-record FASTA), report the short pattern they share, as a consensus, a position-weight matrix and one site per sequence. This is the opposite question from motif_finder, which searches for a pattern you already have. Gibbs site sampler (Lawrence et al., Science 1993), one occurrence per sequence, both strands by default. ⚠️ READ `found` BEFORE THE CONSENSUS: a Gibbs sampler returns a motif from ANY input, including pure noise, because its objective has a maximum whether or not anything is there — so every run is scored against shuffled copies of the same sequences, which hold the same length and base composition and no arrangement. `found` is true only when the real alignment beats every shuffle outright AND clears the control mean by the margin in `control.zScore`; when it is false the consensus and sites are still returned, so you can see what was rejected. Measured: 0 of 20 pure-noise sets were reported as found, and a 10-mer planted in all 12 sequences was recovered exactly on 5 of 5 seeds. The sampler is deterministic — the same input gives the same answer, so a saved or shared result reproduces; pass a different `seed` to see whether the motif survives a different starting point, because one that does not is weak.

bothStrands.description: Allow a site on either strand. A motif has no canonical orientation, so the consensus may come back as the reverse complement of the one you expect.

seed.description: Sampler seed. Fixed by default so one input gives one answer; change it to test whether the motif is stable.

sequences.description: Two or more sequences as multi-record FASTA. Records shorter than the motif width are left out and named in notes. At most 500 sequences and 100,000 residues in total.

width.description: Motif length in bases (4-30). The width is given rather than searched for: trying every width and keeping the best score would select on the same quantity the control measures, and a wider motif scores higher for free.

name: motif_discover
title: Motif Discovery
